facts.detail: The checker uses operator-supplied computer-model coverage predictions.
Ofcom tests predictions with dedicated measurement hardware at sample UK locations.
Predictions are generally reliable but cannot guarantee coverage at a specific point.
Trees, buildings and seasonal foliage can create unmodelled local variation.

guard_streams.write_limit: Predicted mobile coverage cannot establish exact parcel service or current signal.

facts.detail: Ofcom aims to update predictions every three months or with Connected Nations publications.
Operator predictions are combined under a single independent Ofcom standard.
Ofcom results can differ from operator maps because the assessment standard differs.
Average signal strength across a grid can mask variation inside that grid.

guard_streams.write_limit: Update cadence and standards do not create parcel-level certainty.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom broadband and mobile coverage checker

facts.detail: The checkers accept a postcode for mobile predictions or broadband availability.
Broadband results include standard, superfast and ultrafast categories.
Fixed and mobile data are available through an Ofcom developer API.
The checker cannot report maintenance or known local network issues.

guard_streams.write_limit: Checker categories and API data do not prove a live line, orderability or outage-free service.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom Map Your Mobile million-user update

facts.detail: Ofcom reported one million Map Your Mobile users by 29 May 2026.
The service provides postcode-area maps and comparative postal-district scores.
It incorporates crowdsourced Opensignal user-experience data.
It also uses predictive information from UK mobile networks.

guard_streams.write_limit: Crowdsourced and predicted scores are not exact fixed-broadband parcel measurements.

facts.detail: BDUK and FullFibre mutually terminated the Peak District contract.
BDUK stated it was arranging alternative supplier plans.
The area was added to Openreach call-off one in April 2026.
The reassignment records procurement status, not completed service.

guard_streams.write_limit: Termination and reassignment cannot identify ready-for-service parcels.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Nottinghamshire and West Lincolnshire contract

facts.detail: CityFibre is no longer delivering this contract.
BDUK cited wider market conditions and significant commercial expansion.
Less public funding was required and the contract was no longer appropriate.
BDUK is discussing alternatives for remaining premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract termination and commercial plans do not prove current parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: BDUK West Herefordshire and Forest of Dean contract

facts.detail: BDUK and FullFibre mutually terminated the contract.
BDUK stated it was moving to alternative supplier plans.
West Herefordshire was added to Openreach call-off three in April 2026.
The reassignment text specifies West Herefordshire, not all original geography.

guard_streams.write_limit: A partial reassignment cannot be expanded to all original-contract parcels.

facts.detail: The original contract targeted up to 45,000 premises.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 35,000 premises.
The redesigned contract is backed by up to £77 million.
BDUK cited commercial expansion and changed market conditions.

guard_streams.write_limit: Redesigned totals are planning evidence, not exact parcel serviceability.

facts.detail: The original Kent contract targeted around 50,000 premises for £112 million.
The original contract was signed in January 2024.
The May 2026 redesign reduced scope to around 9,000 premises for £26.1 million.
BDUK is discussing options for remaining uncovered premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Redesign and discussions cannot establish current address-level orderability.

facts.detail: BDUK and Freedom Fibre mutually terminated the Cheshire contract.
Freedom Fibre received no public funding for it.
Premises were moved to Openreach call-off eight in February 2026.
Call-off eight awards £37.5 million for around 18,500 premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Reprocurement scope cannot be treated as completed parcel coverage.

facts.detail: The update concerns southwest and central Cornwall Lots 32.02 and 32.03.
Wildanet had covered around 13,200 premises.
Wildanet will not deliver the remaining 7,700 contracted premises.
BDUK is arranging alternative supplier plans.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional totals cannot identify which target parcels are complete.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Dorset and South Somerset contract

facts.detail: Wessex Internet is the awarded supplier.
The contract value is £33.5 million.
The award targets around 21,400 hard-to-reach premises.
It was signed in March 2024; planning and construction precede service.

guard_streams.write_limit: Award scope and planned build do not prove current parcel availability.

facts.detail: The collection summarises local, regional and Openreach framework contracts.
Project Gigabit targets hard-to-reach communities requiring intervention.
The collection links procurement pages rather than a parcel delivery ledger.
Linked pages record redesign, termination and reassignment after awards.

guard_streams.write_limit: A procurement collection cannot serve as exact current parcel evidence.

facts.detail: Ofcom coverage outputs include model predictions and area observations.
BDUK scope records intended intervention and can change.
Ofcom states the checker cannot identify maintenance or local issues.
Neither source family replaces accepted r2 bytes and deterministic postjoin evidence.

guard_streams.write_limit: Cross-source corroboration cannot promote an exact parcel without the canonical join.
